introduction.text: The Chiesa di Santa Maria della Pietà is a Roman Catholic church in Rome’s Borgo district, serving as the national church for Austria, Germany, and the Netherlands. It is historically significant as the site of a medieval hospice for German pilgrims founded by Charlemagne and as a center of German cultural and religious life in Rome.

history.description: In 796 Charlemagne, with permission from Pope Leo III, founded a hospice for German pilgrims adjacent to the site, including a church and burial ground.
During the Avignon Papacy (1309–1378) and the Western Schism, the hospice and surrounding foundations fell into decay.
Under Pope Martin V (1417–1431) the cemetery was expanded and surrounded by a wall built by Fredericus Alemannus.
In 1448, during a plague outbreak, Johannis Assonensis founded a brotherhood to provide burial for poor German pilgrims.
The Holy Year of 1450 saw the brotherhood build a new church and hospice, establishing the Campo Santo as a German national institution.
The present church was constructed in 1501.
During the Sack of Rome in 1527, the Swiss Guard made their last stand in the Teutonic Cemetery, holding off invaders.
In 1876 Pope Pius IX founded a seminary for German-speaking priests to replace the Schola Francorum.
In 1957 a portal by sculptor Elmar Hillebrand was given to the church by German President Theodor Heuss.

design.description: The present church was built in 1501, replacing earlier medieval structures.
The church was remodeled in 1972, updating its interior and exterior.
A portal by sculptor Elmar Hillebrand was installed in 1957, providing access from the cemetery.

art.description: Main altarpiece depicting a Deposition by Polidoro di Caravaggio, flanked by a painting by Giacinto d'Hasse.
Tomb monument of Giacinto d'Hasse inside the church, sculpted by Francois Duquesnoy.
Lateral altar with a St Erasmus by Giacinto Gimignani.
Lateral altar with an Epiphany by Scarsellino.
Altar dedicated to St Charles Borromeo featuring a Flight to Egypt by Arrigo Fiammingo.
Altar with St John Nepomunk by Ignazio Stern.
Sacristy holds an Immaculate Conception by Luigi Garzi.
